text:
omar: Heads-up — after the recent prefix/KV packing change on canary I'm seeing a reproducible p99 spike (~150ms) on short completion requests. Not traffic volume, looks queueing related.

julia: ugh, saw something similar in perf dashboards last night. Any flamegraphs?

omar: quick snapshot from the canary trace:
```
queue_wait_ms: 42
batch_formation_ms: 21
kernel_exec_ms: 6-12 (varies)
kv_lookup_ms: 0-1
pack_policy: HIT_AWARE_PACKER
selected_kernel: attn_fused_fast
fallback_kernel: attn_generic (when seq>ctx)
```

omar: interesting bit — when packer packs many hit-prefix requests together the token-budget heuristic seems to inflate batches even when effective kernel exec stays small. We end up waiting longer for a full token budget before sending.

kevin: does this only show up for short sequences? or also long contexts?

omar: mostly short completions (<=8 gen tokens) with long prefixes where kv-hit ratio > 0.8. Latency goes up because the packer expects larger batch token budget and waits.

sarah: could be the token_budget_target math — we recently changed default from 2048->3072 for hit-aware mode, right?

julia: yep, that was the change. The idea was to improve throughput for mixed lengths but might backfire for low-token infer requests.

perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: canary-2026-03-16 - p99 latency +35% for route /generate-short on model rdx-small-quant. Trace id 0x7fae2c.

kevin: hypothesis: hit-aware packer multiplies token_budget by (1 + est_hit_prefix_frac) — if est_hit_prefix_frac is high it overshoots. Combined with our batch_timeout smoothing it delays release.

omar: test I ran: force token_budget_target to 1024 for hit-aware packer -> p99 returns to baseline. So config is the immediate knob.

julia: nice repro. Can you paste the small patch to the packer config you used?

omar: sure, diff:
```
- token_budget_target = base_target * (1 + hit_frac)
+ token_budget_target = min(base_target * (1 + hit_frac), base_target * 1.25)
```

omar: with that cap p99 stable and throughput unaffected on mixed workloads in local replay.

sarah: two thoughts: (1) short-term revert/cap in canary config, (2) longer-term: change admission policy to prefer latency SLOs for routes tagged `latency-sensitive`.

kevin: agree. Also want to check kernel selection interplay — when batch grows but still all kv-hits kernel_exec is tiny; but if packer mixes a few cold prefixes we might hit fallback kernels (attn_generic) which blow up exec time and amplify waiting. Need to detect heterogenous kernel costs at formation time.

julia: maybe add a quick per-request kernel_cost_estimate (based on seq len + quantization profile) and compute a weighted token_budget in packer. Simpler: don't aggregate requests whose kernel_cost variance > threshold.

omar: I'll open a tiny canary patch: cap token_budget + don't co-pack requests with kernel_cost_sd > 0.2. Will run replay across 3 traffic shapes.

perf-bot: scheduled replay job: replay-1919876543-1 queued.

omar: tagging @oncall-eng in case we decide to flip canary back during business hours.

sarah: thanks — prioritize quick cap, then iterate on the variance-based admission. Good catch. :thumbsup:

kevin: logging request-level `estimated_kernel` in packer will help future debugging, add a small histogram in console.

omar: noted. will send PR + canary run results in this thread in ~30m.

julia: awesome. if you need a hand with replay config ping me.
